spatial_claims.claim: Point C lies on segment AB between A and B, dividing it into sub-segments AC and CB, constructed by 2.11 so that rect(AB, BC) = sq(AC)
AB = AC + CB (C is between A and B, so the segment is additively decomposed)
AC is the greater segment and BC is the lesser segment (AC > BC)

configuration_map: The configuration consists of a single line segment AB with one interior point C. Point C is placed by Proposition 2.11 so that rect(AB, BC) = sq(AC). This forces the ratio AC/BC = (1+sqrt(5))/2 (golden ratio), meaning C lies between A and B, closer to B, with AC approximately 61.8% of AB and BC approximately 38.2% of AB. The entire geometry is collinear with no auxiliary constructions, triangles, circles, or angles involved.
pass_reason: The proof's spatial content is minimal and trivially consistent: one point C on one line segment AB, with all claims (C between A and B, AC greater than BC) following necessarily from the 2.11 construction. There are no angle decompositions, no interior/exterior claims, no complex geometric configurations where contradictions could arise. The proof is primarily algebraic/proportional.
